name: Art Deco Quarter
tagline: The rebuilt centre, walkable and full of 1930s facades
description: The heart of the town Napier rebuilt in a single style after the 1931 earthquake, a compact grid of pastel Art Deco frontages along Tennyson and Emerson Streets. Cafes, the MTG museum and most of the shops are here, and almost everything is within a ten-minute walk.
bestFor: Anyone who wants to work without a car and be in the middle of the town
pros: The best cafes and the museum are here
Fibre is available across the centre
cons: Quiet after early evening on weekdays
Fills completely during the February Art Deco Festival
Apartment stock is limited above the shops

name: Bluff Hill
tagline: The headland above the port with the views
description: The hill rising behind Marine Parade towards the port, a residential area of older houses on steep streets with views over Hawke Bay and the container terminal. It is a five-minute drive or a stiff walk from the centre, and it is where the town's best outlook is.
bestFor: People staying a while who want a house and a view rather than a flat in town
pros: Views over the bay and the port
Minutes from the centre by car
cons: The gradients are serious on foot
Port noise reaches parts of the hill
Little in the way of shops or cafes

name: Ahuriri
tagline: The old port basin turned into the town's restaurant strip
description: The inner harbour district a few minutes northwest of the centre, where the old wool stores have become apartments and the waterfront carries most of Napier's better restaurants and bars. The marina and West Quay are the focus, and the cycle trails start here.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the best eating and drinking within walking distance
pros: The strongest restaurant and bar cluster in town
Cycle trails begin at the door
cons: More expensive than the rest of Napier
A twenty-minute walk from the Art Deco centre
Exposed and windy in bad weather

name: Taradale
tagline: Suburban, cheaper and closer to the vineyards
description: A suburb about ten minutes inland with its own small shopping centre, the regional institute of technology and a quieter residential feel. Rents drop noticeably here and the wine country around Church Road and the Taradale hills starts at the edge of the neighbourhood.
bestFor: Longer stays where price matters more than being in the centre
pros: Cheaper rents than the centre or Ahuriri

name: Marewa
tagline: Art Deco housing away from the tourist streets
description: A residential suburb south of the centre laid out after the earthquake, which is why it holds one of the largest concentrations of Art Deco houses anywhere. It is ordinary, affordable and entirely local, with the Kennedy Park end backing onto sports fields and the airport road.
bestFor: Anyone renting a whole house rather than a flat, on a budget
pros: Ten minutes from both the centre and Taradale
cons: Nothing to do within walking distance
Very quiet, which some find dull
